dedupe_keys.name: tud industrial database v1 1 techno economic data for germany s process industry

description: The TUD Industrial Database supports modelling of transformation pathways in Germany's process industry with techno-economic data for conventional and low-carbon production of 22 main outputs, among them alumina, ammonia, bricks, chlorine, clinker, container and float glass, high value chemicals, methanol, paper grades, primary aluminium and copper, primary and secondary steel, quicklime, soda ash and urea. The OPARA repository and DataCite records say the data cover availability factors and lifetimes of process facilities, normalised investments for new and retrofitted plants and further parameters. It was published on 3 June 2025 (version 1.1) by Hendrik Scharf of TU Dresden as one Excel file of about 1.83 MB, free to download under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so commercial use and derivatives are not allowed. Coverage is Germany. Caveats: the price base year and data sources are not stated in the part of the record read, and the no-derivatives licence limits sharing adapted versions. For simulation it gives plant-level parameters to model investment and switching in German heavy industry and the energy and hydrogen demand that follows. Related catalogue records include the TIMES-Sweden Industry Database and the Mopo Industry Technology Catalogue.
